behaviours.summary: An RQ1 request for 256 bytes stops the unit responding entirely, including its Active Sensing. Recovery needs a power cycle.
A one-byte RQ1 at 0C 00 00 is not a read. The unit replies about a different address and then keeps transmitting for 29 seconds, 286 messages in total.
A reply's arrival time grows with its length, but length does not determine it: two addresses that both return 64 bytes answer in 31 ms and 78 ms.

Twelve control changes land in part 1's block at 40 11 xx, each keeping the transmitted value unchanged. Eighteen others, including modulation, expression, hold and delay send, change nothing anywhere in the readable address space.

The map bounds the rhythm part block's first region at 26 bytes, ending at 40 10 19, and an oversize read there is refused. The twelve addresses above it, 40 10 1A through 25, all answer a single-byte read and all hold their own values.
Adjacent addresses with the same 0 to 7 range disagree on what happens outside it. 40 01 30, 31 and 38 leave their value untouched; 40 01 32 and 39 clamp to 07.
40 01 41 through 47 return nothing to an RQ1 addressed at them, yet their contents come back in a read that starts earlier.

rule.reachedBy: a read that starts earlier in the same region

behaviours.summary: About two probes in a hundred come back as one frame that starts with F0 and ends with F7 but is not one SysEx message: an unterminated header, then three byte groups led by EF, then the correct reply. Re-asking after the path goes quiet always produced a clean reply.
CC10 hard pan fully separates a mono patch but leaves a stereo patch's internal spread largely intact.

CC0 and CC32 change nothing readable on their own. A program change commits the three of them together, and only if that bank holds that program: otherwise the whole triple is discarded and the bank byte, the program byte and the map byte all keep the values they had. A bank left latched therefore switches off every later program change silently, because the latch itself is in no readable address.

rule.discardedNote: A triple the unit does not have is discarded whole, and the latch itself is in no readable address — so a bank left latched switches off every later program change with nothing to read that says so.

behaviours.summary: Every GS part NRPN this unit answers is stored in the same byte as a control change, verbatim on both routes. The pair is not merely two names for one parameter: it is one storage location with two ways in.
RPN 00 05 is kept at 40 21 04 as floor(sent * 127 / 6), saturating at 127. It is the only one of the four GS RPNs that reaches any readable address, and the only alias so far that is not verbatim.

A DT1 write reaches every byte a control change and an NRPN were measured to reach, keeping the value verbatim, and moves nothing else anywhere in the readable map. So each of these parameters has one storage location with three ways in and no mirror. The three routes are not interchangeable: RPN 00 05 converts on the way in while a DT1 to the same byte does not, so the scaling belongs to the receiver rather than to the storage.

GS Reset returns all 37502 readable bytes to exactly what the unit held after a power cycle. GM1 System On leaves 88 of them elsewhere and GM2 System On leaves 974, and the two GM resets are not nested: they share 32 changes, GM1 makes 56 the other does not, and GM2 makes 942 the other does not. All three restore every marked byte, so the difference is not in what they reset but in what they additionally set.

Asking for all 16384 bank and program combinations on map 0 finds 1710 tones in 53 banks. Bank 0 holds a full 128. The variation banks thin out from there, down to bank 47 holding one tone and bank 48 holding one. Banks 64, 65 and 127 accept every program and bank 126 accepts exactly 0 to 63.

Two takes of the same note, aligned to a fraction of a sample and levelled, differ by 54 dB less than the note itself, which is 0.1 to 2.3 dB above what the converter noise alone would leave. What actually fails to repeat is -58 dB down. The level agrees to under 0.001 dB. The trigger arrives within a 4 ms window, so the alignment is doing real work rather than confirming a timing that was already good.

CC7 at 40 against 127 changes the level by 20.09 dB and leaves the shape of the note otherwise untouched. A square law, amplitude proportional to the square of the value, predicts 40 log10(127/40) = 20.07 dB. The two agree to 0.02 dB.

CC91 at 0 against 100 changes the sound by 26 to 50 dB more than two takes of one setting differ, under all five stimuli, and takes with the reverb on repeat as well as dry ones. So the reverb reaches the signal path and holds no moving part. CC93 at 0 against 100 does the opposite: it leaves no residual that clears the yardstick, and instead destroys repeatability. What fails to repeat rises from between -41.6 and -63.3 dB dry to between -1.9 and -3.9 dB with the chorus on, under every one of the five. The chorus carries a modulator at a different phase each time the note is struck.

Seven voices were held for 20 seconds each at A above middle C and their frequency taken from the slope of the unwrapped phase. All seven wobble: the phase departs from a straight line by 0.09 to 2.8 cycles, so none is a frequency reference. Their pitches span 466 ppm flat to 2842 ppm sharp of equal temperament at A440, with master tune at its default, so the spread is the voices rather than the tuning.

A part switched to rhythm mode accepts a chorus send, stores it verbatim and reads it back, and sounds no different for it. The reverb send on the same part in the same run is plainly audible. This is a property of rhythm mode rather than of part 10: part 2 hears the chorus while it is melodic and stops hearing it once USE FOR RHYTHM PART is set, with nothing else changed.

Excited with a broadband unpitched note, the reverb's decay falls smoothly from 2.10 s at 63 Hz to 1.03 s at 8 kHz, the top decaying 2.04 times faster than the bottom. Every band is straight, departing from its fitted line by 0.17 to 0.89 dB. Excited with a piano note instead, the same reverb reads 1.69, 2.09, 1.41, 2.44, 1.62, 1.90, 1.52 and 0.87 s -- a scatter several times wider than each band's own bound, in no order.

A melodic part block holds 47 addresses. 46 can be asked at two settings the unit accepts; 40 1n 17 accepts one value only and cannot be asked at all. Of the 46, 20 changed the sound and 26 did not under anything tried. Parts 1, 2 and 3 were each swept in full and returned the same 20, address for address. The rhythm part's block is not the same block: the map bounds it at 35 addresses, 34 askable, of which 10 changed the sound.

At panpot 127 the two channels the unit arrives on sit at -58.6 and -48.4 dB on every take, agreeing to 0.1 dB. At panpot 0 the same four takes land at -54.5/-49.3, -47.3/-62.9, -52.2/-50.6 and -63.7/-47.4 dB: a balance spanning over 31 dB while the two channels together stay within 1.21 dB. The placement is different on every note struck; the loudness is not.

With modulation held at 127, the note's own frequency is modulated at 12.73 Hz on all four takes with 40 11 30 set to 127, and no modulation is found at all with it set to 0. Left at its power-on value the same measurement reads 4.11 Hz, taken from the takes of a different address in the same block, and 4.11 to 4.52 Hz from those of another.

Two notes at once, and one note struck twice 0.4 s apart, were built to ask the questions a single note cannot put. Neither repeats: the plain note's takes agree within -56 to -62 dB, while the struck-again stimulus lands between -1.1 and -66 dB with 84 per cent of its figures worse than -10 dB. No verdict taken from either survived being asked a second time.

A swept sine played into the analogue input comes back flat within 0.1 dB from 63 Hz to 8 kHz with distortion 86 dB down. The insertion effect, the system reverb and the system chorus were each raised as far as they go, and the returned sweep moved by 0.2, 0.5 and 0.2 dB. Each was raised with a control proving the same state changes a note the machine plays.

Of the twenty parameter addresses one insertion effect type loads, ten changed the sound, nine did not under the note asked, and one broke the repeatability it would have been measured against instead of changing anything the comparison could see. The type-level sort passed all sixty-five types the unit has, so it turned nothing away; asked at the parameter, the same question retires nine addresses of twenty.

A note the first output pair carried 58 dB over the silence before it left the second pair at the line inputs' own noise floor, -107.5 dB, with no note in it. The first pair was measured immediately before and immediately after the change and answered the same both times.

40 42 21 accepts 00 to 03 and holds 00. At 00 the part sounds on the first output pair and not the second; at 01 it sounds on the second and not the first. On the second pair neither the insertion effect nor the system reverb changes it, while a volume controller does.

Reading one byte past every region the map holds, and on forward where one answered: of the 85 regions under the block the parameters live in, four run past their mapped size, 29 addresses in all. Two of them are in the insertion effect's own block. Across the whole map 660 of 854 regions run past their end, but 480 of those are the twelve blocks already established to be a window, which answer at any address.

Reading all 128 offsets of one block, a byte at a time, left the unit answering nothing -- not the address the run was asking about, not the address it carried as a control, and not an identity request. It did not come back on its own and was recovered by switching it off and on.

Of the 128 offsets in one part's assign block, five answer a single-byte read: 00 and 01, which the map holds, and 20, 21 and 22, which it does not. A second such block answers at the same five offsets. 21 is the byte that moves the part to the second output pair and 22 the byte that routes it through the insertion effect.

The insertion effect's block answers to 40 03 1F and not to 40 03 20, so it holds 32 addresses where the map gives it 30. Of the nine above the twenty parameters, three change the sound and five do not; one accepts a single value and cannot be asked. One of the three removes the repeatability it would be read against.

The reverb half of 40 01 was asked with a send raised on part 1 while the stimulus sounded on part 10, so the preparation reached nothing the note went through. Its verdicts stand anyway: the reverb was already reached through the send every part powers up holding, and raising part 10's own send to full changes no answer.

Polyphonic pressure at 127 against 0, on the note the stimulus was already sounding, is inaudible on this unit under power-on defaults. That is the control the receive switch over the message needs and cannot supply itself: a null taken by moving the switch cannot say whether the switch is silent or the message it gates does nothing to listen to.

Offset 12 of the part block answered on all three melodic parts asked, and only under a stimulus carrying a soft pedal and nothing else. It had read as inaudible on every part until then, across four earlier passes, because no gesture in the catalogue sent that controller at all.
